title: Rule 1 · Aim & Structure of the Game (Art. 1.1)
prompt: Under Official FIBA Basketball Rules Article 1.1, how many players per team are on the court during standard play, and which personnel jointly conduct the game?

options.optionLabel: A. 5 players each; conducted by referees, table officials, and a commissioner (if present)
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 1.1): Basketball is played by 2 teams of 5 players each, conducted by the referees, table officials and a commissioner (including technical delegate), if present.

options.optionLabel: B. 5 players each; conducted strictly by the Crew Chief without table official input
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 1.1): Both teams have 5 players on the floor, and the game is conducted by referees, table officials, and a commissioner if present.

options.optionLabel: C. 6 players each; conducted by 2 referees and coaches
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 1.1): Basketball teams field 5 players on court, and coaches do not officiate the game.

options.optionLabel: D. 5 players each; winner is decided solely by number of field goals made
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 1.4): Winner is the team with the greater number of points (1, 2, or 3 points per goal), not total baskets made.

title: Rule 1 · Participants’ Responsibility (Art. 1.2)
prompt: During the 3rd quarter, a team coach and scorer notice a scoreboard error showing 2 extra points awarded to Team A. Under 2026 Art. 1.2 (Participants’ responsibility), what must participants do?

options.optionLabel: A. Notify the referees immediately upon becoming aware of the correctable inaccuracy
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 1.2): All participants, table officials, commissioners, players, coaches and delegation members must uphold ethical behaviour and notify the referees immediately if aware of a correctable inaccuracy in score, fouls, time-outs, or clock operations.

options.optionLabel: B. Wait until the end of the game to file a written protest (Appendix C) even if noticed in Q3
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 1.2): Participants are explicitly required to notify referees immediately when becoming aware of an inaccuracy rather than waiting.

options.optionLabel: C. Ask the timekeeper to subtract the points silently during live play
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 1.2 & Art. 44): Table officials cannot unilaterally change official score without reporting to the Crew Chief/referees.

options.optionLabel: D. Ignore errors made by the opposing team’s benefit but report only own disadvantages
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 1.2): Ethical responsibility applies equally to all participants regardless of which team benefits.

title: Rule 1 · Own Basket vs Opponents’ Basket (Art. 1.3)
prompt: According to Article 1.3 and Article 16, what happens if Player B1 accidentally taps the ball into B1’s OWN basket while trying to rebound a missed shot?

options.optionLabel: A. 2 points are awarded to Team A and recorded to the captain on the court of Team A
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 1.3 & Art. 16.2.2): The basket defended by Team B is B’s own basket. If a player accidentally scores in their own basket, the goal counts 2 points for the opponents (Team A) and is recorded for Team A’s captain on the court.

options.optionLabel: B. Goal is cancelled and possession goes to Team B by alternating possession
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 16.2.2): Accidental own-basket goals count 2 points for the opponents (only deliberate own-basket scoring is a violation).

options.optionLabel: C. 3 points are awarded if B1 was outside the 3-point arc when tipping
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 16.2.2): An accidental goal in one’s own basket always counts as 2 points regardless of position.

options.optionLabel: D. Points are recorded individually under B1’s foul column
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 16.2.2): The 2 points are credited to the opposing captain on the court.

title: Rule 1 · Winner of a Game (Art. 1.4)
prompt: At the end of the fourth quarter, the score is tied 78–78. Under Article 1.4 and Article 8.7, how is the winner determined?

options.optionLabel: A. Play as many 5-minute overtimes as needed until one team leads at the end of an extra period
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 1.4 & Art. 8.7): If the score is tied at the end of the 4th quarter, the game continues with as many 5-minute overtimes as necessary to break the tie (unless competition rules mandate home-and-away aggregate ties).

options.optionLabel: B. Sudden-death first basket wins immediately in overtime
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 8.7): Standard FIBA basketball never uses sudden-death in overtime; each overtime lasts 5 full minutes.

options.optionLabel: C. Three-round free-throw shootout between captains
options.explanation: Incorrect: Basketball does not use free-throw shootouts.

options.optionLabel: D. Team with fewer accumulated team fouls is declared the winner
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 1.4): Winner is strictly the team with the greater number of points.

title: Rule 2 · Court Dimensions & Boundary Lines (Art. 2.1–2.2)
prompt: What are the official FIBA court dimensions measured from the inner edge of the boundary lines, and are the boundary lines part of the playing court?

options.optionLabel: A. 28 m × 15 m; boundary lines are NOT part of the playing court (touching them is out-of-bounds)
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 2.1 & Art. 2.2.1): A FIBA playing court is 28 m long by 15 m wide from the inner edges of the boundary lines. Boundary lines themselves are out-of-bounds and NOT part of the playing court.

options.optionLabel: B. 28 m × 15 m; boundary lines ARE part of the playing court until both feet cross outside
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.2.1): Boundary lines are out-of-bounds; touching any part of the boundary line puts a player or ball out of bounds.

options.optionLabel: C. 26 m × 14 m; sideline is in-bounds while endline is out-of-bounds
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.1): Standard FIBA dimensions are 28 m × 15 m, and both sidelines and endlines are out-of-bounds.

options.optionLabel: D. 30 m × 16 m; lines are 10 cm wide and part of the restricted area
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.2): Lines are 5 cm wide on a 28 m × 15 m court.

title: Rule 2 · No-Charge Semi-Circle Measurements & Lines (Art. 2.4.7)
prompt: What is the radius of the FIBA no-charge semi-circle measured from the point on the floor directly beneath the centre of the basket, and is the semi-circle line itself part of the area?

options.optionLabel: A. 1.30 m radius; YES — the painted semi-circle line IS part of the no-charge semi-circle area
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 2.4.7 & Art. 33.10): The no-charge semi-circle has a 1.30 m radius from the projection of the basket centre, and the semi-circle line IS part of the no-charge area (touching the line with any foot places the defender inside).

options.optionLabel: B. 1.25 m radius; NO — like boundary lines, the semi-circle line is outside the zone
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.4.7): Notice the key rulebook rule — the no-charge semi-circle has a 1.30 m radius AND its line IS part of the semi-circle area (unlike the 3-point line or boundary lines).

options.optionLabel: C. 1.50 m radius; applies only during the final 2 minutes of the 4th quarter
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.4.7 & Art. 33.10): The radius is 1.30 m and applies throughout all periods.

options.optionLabel: D. 1.80 m radius matching the free-throw circle
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.4.4 & Art. 2.4.7): The free-throw circle radius is 1.80 m; the no-charge semi-circle is 1.30 m.

title: Rule 2 · Three-Point Line & Restricted Area Line Status (Art. 2.4.4)
prompt: What is the distance of the FIBA 3-point arc from the projection of the basket centre, and if a shooter’s toe touches the painted 3-point line on take-off, what is the shot’s value?

options.optionLabel: A. 6.75 m radius (6.60 m straight sideline minimum); 2 points because the line is part of the 2-point area
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 2.4.4 & Art. 16.2.1): The 3-point arc is 6.75 m (straight sidelines at 6.60 m). The 3-point line itself is NOT part of the 3-point area, so touching it makes the shot a 2-point attempt.

options.optionLabel: B. 6.75 m radius; 3 points because any contact with the line favors the shooter
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.4.4): The 3-point line belongs to the 2-point field goal area.

options.optionLabel: C. 7.24 m radius uniformly around the court
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.4.4): 7.24 m is NBA, not FIBA (6.75 m).

options.optionLabel: D. 6.25 m radius; 3 points if released above 2.90 m
options.explanation: Incorrect: FIBA increased the arc from 6.25 m to 6.75 m.

title: Rule 2 · Centre Line Frontcourt/Backcourt Status & Equipment (Art. 2.4.1 & Art. 3)
prompt: Which side of the court does the centre line belong to, and at what game-clock threshold must both game clock and shot clock show tenths of a second?

options.optionLabel: A. Centre line is part of the BACKCOURT; game clock displays tenths under 1 minute (60.0s) and shot clock under 5 seconds (5.0s)
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 2.4.1 & Art. 3): The centre line is part of the backcourt. Under Art. 3 (Equipment / Timing), the game clock displays tenths of a second during the last 60 seconds of a quarter/overtime, and the shot clock displays tenths during the last 5 seconds.

options.optionLabel: B. Centre line belongs to the frontcourt; tenths display only under 10 seconds
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.4.1): The centre line is always part of the backcourt.

options.optionLabel: C. Centre line is neutral until the player finishes dribbling
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 2.4.1): Touching the centre line keeps the player/ball in the backcourt.

options.optionLabel: D. Shot clock displays tenths throughout all 24 seconds
options.explanation: Incorrect: Tenths of a second on the shot clock are shown during the final 5 seconds.

title: Rule 3 · Team Composition & 12-Player Roster (Art. 4.2)
prompt: How many team members entitled to play may be listed on the scoresheet before a FIBA game, and what is the maximum number of team followers (including coaches) permitted on the team bench area?

options.optionLabel: A. Maximum 12 players entitled to play (plus up to 8 team bench staff — head coach, up to 2 assistant coaches, max 8 total)
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 4.2.1): Each team consists of no more than 12 team members entitled to play (including a captain), a head coach, and up to a maximum of 8 accompanying delegation members who may sit on the team bench (with specific responsibilities).

options.optionLabel: B. Unlimited players on scoresheet as long as only 10 dress in uniform
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 4.2.1): Maximum 12 players entitled to play.

options.optionLabel: C. Maximum 15 players in 5-on-5 FIBA official competitions
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 4.2.1): FIBA 5-on-5 team roster limit is 12.

options.optionLabel: D. Coaches sit across from the opposing bench rather than within the team bench area
options.explanation: Incorrect: Each team sits in its designated bench area with its own basket defended in the 1st half.

title: Rule 3 · Uniforms, Socks & Undershirts (Art. 4.3 & Art. 4.4)
prompt: Under Article 4.3 and 4.4 of the 2026 FIBA Rules, what is required regarding compression sleeves/leggings, socks, and jewelry/headwear during a game?

options.optionLabel: A. Compression gear/accessories must be solid black, white, or the same dominant colour as shorts/shirts (consistent per team); dangerous jewelry/objects prohibited
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 4.4.2): All team members using arm/leg compression sleeves, headbands, or wristbands must have them in the same solid colour (black, white, or dominant uniform colour). Watches, necklaces, earrings, or dangerous objects are strictly prohibited.

options.optionLabel: B. Players may wear mismatched neon compression sleeves and taped metal rings
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 4.4.2): Jewelry may NOT simply be taped over if dangerous, and accessories must match uniformly across team members.

options.optionLabel: C. Playing numbers 00 and 0–99 are barred except 4–15
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 4.3.2): FIBA permits jersey numbers 0, 00, and 1–99.

options.optionLabel: D. T-shirts worn under jerseys may be any colour regardless of jersey colour
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 4.4.2): Undershirts may not extend below the jersey and compression shirts follow strict matching uniform colour rules.

title: Rule 3 · Player Injury & 15-Second / Blood Rule (Art. 5)
prompt: When play is stopped because a player is injured (and a coach/doctor steps onto the court or treatment exceeds ~15 seconds), what MUST happen unless the team calls a legal time-out?

options.optionLabel: A. The injured player MUST be substituted (unless a time-out is granted and they recover before the end of it)
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 5.2–5.4): If the game is stopped for an injured player who cannot continue within ~15 seconds or receives treatment/court entry by coach/medical staff, that player MUST be substituted — unless the team takes a charged time-out and the player recovers before it ends.

options.optionLabel: B. The injured player gets an automatic 3-minute medical pause without substitution or time-out
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 5.3): FIBA enforces the 15-second / court-assistance mandatory substitution rule.

options.optionLabel: C. A technical foul is always charged for stopping the game with an injury
options.explanation: Incorrect: Genuine injury stoppages do not incur a technical foul.

options.optionLabel: D. Opponents choose which substitute replaces the injured free-throw shooter
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 5.6): The injured player’s coach selects the substitute (from eligible bench players).

title: Rule 3 · Captain & Head Coach Duties (Art. 6 & Art. 7)
prompt: Who is permitted to stand inside the team bench area during live play, and who signs the scoresheet if a team submits a protest at the end of the game?

options.optionLabel: A. Only the Head Coach (not assistant coaches simultaneously) may remain standing; the CAPTAIN (or acting captain) signs the scoresheet to file a protest
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 6.2 & Art. 7.7): Only the Head Coach is permitted to stand during the game within the team bench area. Only the Captain (or acting captain if captain has left the court) may sign the scoresheet under protest.

options.optionLabel: B. Both Head Coach and First Assistant Coach may stand together; the Head Coach signs protests
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 6.2 & Art. 7.7): Only one person (Head Coach) may remain standing; protests on the scoresheet are signed by the Captain.

options.optionLabel: C. Any substitute may stand to yell instructions; team manager signs protests
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 7.7): Substitutes must remain seated except when waiting to enter.

options.optionLabel: D. Captain loses all speaking rights once the coach receives a warning
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 6.1): The captain remains the on-court representative in a courteous manner.

title: Appendix B · Scoresheet Recording Codes (B / T / D / DI / F)
prompt: Under the 2026 FIBA Official Rules and Appendix B, what new foul symbol is entered on the scoresheet for an Article 37 Disruptive Foul, and does it count toward 2-foul Game Disqualification (GD)?

options.optionLabel: A. Entered as DI; it does NOT count toward the 2-foul GD ejection (though it counts toward a player’s 5 fouls and team fouls)
options.explanation: Correct (Art. 37.2 & App. B): In 2026 FIBA rules, Disruptive fouls replace transition/clock unsportsmanlike calls (former C3/C4/C5), are marked DI on the scoresheet, do NOT count toward 2-foul GD ejection, and still count toward 5 personal fouls + team bonus.

options.optionLabel: B. Entered as U2; two DI fouls automatically eject the player under GD
options.explanation: Incorrect (Art. 37.2): Flagrant fouls (F) and Technical fouls (T) combine for GD; Disruptive fouls (DI) do NOT count toward GD.

options.optionLabel: C. Entered as B1; never counts toward team foul bonus
options.explanation: Incorrect: Every player foul (personal, DI, F) counts toward the team foul count in that quarter.

options.optionLabel: D. Entered only in the coach’s box and does not count toward 5 fouls
options.explanation: Incorrect: DI is charged to the player and counts toward their 5-foul disqualification limit.

title: Appendix C · Official Protest Procedure Timing
prompt: Under Appendix C, what are the strict steps and timelines for a team to submit a valid protest after the end of a game?

options.optionLabel: A. Captain informs Crew Chief immediately (signs "Captain’s signature in case of protest" within 15 min); detailed written reasons + fee follow within 1 hour
options.explanation: Correct (Appendix C): The captain must immediately inform the Crew Chief at game end and sign the scoresheet within 15 minutes after the game ends; written confirmation of reasons must be submitted within 1 hour.

options.optionLabel: B. Head Coach emails FIBA within 48 hours without signing the scoresheet
options.explanation: Incorrect (Appendix C): Without the captain signing the scoresheet within 15 minutes at game end, the protest is inadmissible.

options.optionLabel: C. Protests may be used solely to challenge whether a call was a block or charge
options.explanation: Incorrect (Appendix C): Referees’ judgment calls cannot be protested unless an error of rule eligibility/administration occurred.

options.optionLabel: D. Team has 10 seconds before the final horn to submit a written protest form
options.explanation: Incorrect (Appendix C): The signature happens immediately after the game (max 15 min) and written grounds within 1 hour.

title: Appendix D & E · Classification Points & Media Time-Outs
prompt: Under Appendix D (Classification of Teams), how many standings points are awarded for a Win, a Loss by playing, a Loss by Forfeit, and a Loss by Default?

options.optionLabel: A. Win = 2 pts, Played Loss = 1 pt, Default Loss = 1 pt (or 0 in some forfeit), Forfeit Loss = 0 pts (20–0)
options.explanation: Correct (Appendix D.1 & Art. 20–21): A team receives 2 points for each game won, 1 point for each game lost (including lost by default under Art. 21), and 0 points for a game lost by forfeit (Art. 20, 20–0 score).

options.optionLabel: B. Win = 3 pts, Draw = 1 pt, Forfeit = 1 pt
options.explanation: Incorrect (Appendix D.1): FIBA games have no draws and award 2/1/0 points.

options.optionLabel: C. Win = 2 pts, Loss = 0 pts regardless of whether played or forfeited
options.explanation: Incorrect: A played loss earns 1 classification point; a forfeit earns 0.

options.optionLabel: D. Ties in standings are always broken first by 3-point percentage
options.explanation: Incorrect (Appendix D.1): Ties between teams with equal points are broken first by head-to-head results (game points, then head-to-head point difference, then head-to-head points scored).

title: Case A1178 · Act of shooting
ruleReference: Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)
prompt: Watch video case A1178 (Act of shooting). Analyze the player positions, timing, and contact/footwork shown in the clip, then select the correct Official FIBA 2026 call.

options.optionLabel: A. Unsportsmanlike foul on the shooting defender
options.explanation: Incorrect — No offensive charge/unsportsmanlike occurred. Official Ruling: Official Case A1178 (Act of shooting · Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)): After releasing the shot, White 6 extends his leg forward in an attempt to draw a shooting foul, then falls backward in a theatrical manner. He initiates the contact with the defender’s leg; however, since the defender is not disadvantaged, a "no-call" is appropriate. Nevertheless, the shooter must be warned that a recurrence will result in a technical foul.

options.optionLabel: B. Warning for faking/acting (no technical foul yet unless repeated) or no-call if minimal
options.explanation: Correct — Official Case A1178 (Act of shooting · Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)): After releasing the shot, White 6 extends his leg forward in an attempt to draw a shooting foul, then falls backward in a theatrical manner. He initiates the contact with the defender’s leg; however, since the defender is not disadvantaged, a "no-call" is appropriate. Nevertheless, the shooter must be warned that a recurrence will result in a technical foul.

options.optionLabel: C. Immediate disqualification for simulation
options.explanation: Incorrect — Under Art. 36.2.1 / OBRI fake procedures, an official issues a fake warning on first minor simulation without immediate T unless repeated. Official Ruling: Official Case A1178 (Act of shooting · Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)): After releasing the shot, White 6 extends his leg forward in an attempt to draw a shooting foul, then falls backward in a theatrical manner. He initiates the contact with the defender’s leg; however, since the defender is not disadvantaged, a "no-call" is appropriate. Nevertheless, the shooter must be warned that a recurrence will result in a technical foul.

options.optionLabel: D. Offensive charging foul plus 2 free throws to the defense
options.explanation: Incorrect — Simulation first draws a warning (or technical if repeated/blatant), never automatic disqualification. Official Ruling: Official Case A1178 (Act of shooting · Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)): After releasing the shot, White 6 extends his leg forward in an attempt to draw a shooting foul, then falls backward in a theatrical manner. He initiates the contact with the defender’s leg; however, since the defender is not disadvantaged, a "no-call" is appropriate. Nevertheless, the shooter must be warned that a recurrence will result in a technical foul.

title: Case B461 · Travelling
prompt: Watch video case B461 (Travelling). Analyze the player positions, timing, and contact/footwork shown in the clip, then select the correct Official FIBA 2026 call.

options.optionLabel: A. Legal gather step (0-1-2) under FIBA Art. 25.2.1 — play continues / basket counts
options.explanation: Incorrect — The ball handler exceeded legal pivot-foot or 2-step limits after gaining control. Official Ruling: Official Case B461 (Travelling · Art. 24–25 (Dribbling & Travelling)): Travelling? If so, when? There is a travel at the start of the dribble, the pivoting while scoring is legal.

options.optionLabel: B. Normal defensive personal foul on the perimeter defender
options.explanation: Incorrect — There was no illegal defensive contact justifying the extra steps. Official Ruling: Official Case B461 (Travelling · Art. 24–25 (Dribbling & Travelling)): Travelling? If so, when? There is a travel at the start of the dribble, the pivoting while scoring is legal.

options.optionLabel: C. Kicked-ball violation resetting the shot clock to 14 seconds
options.explanation: Incorrect — This is a ball-handling footwork infraction, not a kicked-ball violation. Official Ruling: Official Case B461 (Travelling · Art. 24–25 (Dribbling & Travelling)): Travelling? If so, when? There is a travel at the start of the dribble, the pivoting while scoring is legal.

options.optionLabel: D. Travelling violation — turn over possession to opponents at nearest out-of-bounds spot
options.explanation: Correct — Official Case B461 (Travelling · Art. 24–25 (Dribbling & Travelling)): Travelling? If so, when? There is a travel at the start of the dribble, the pivoting while scoring is legal.

title: Case B460 · Backcourt
prompt: Video Case B460 (Backcourt): Backcourt violation? Watch the clip and choose the correct ruling.

options.optionLabel: A. No backcourt violation — legal play (frontcourt control not established or deflected by defense)
options.explanation: Correct — Official Case B460 (Backcourt · Art. 30 (Ball Returned to Backcourt)): Backcourt violation? Player 4 has not yet gone into the frontcourt, as he have not yet touched the frontcourt with both feet; therefore, a backcourt violation could not have occurred.

options.optionLabel: B. Backcourt violation — opponents’ throw-in in their frontcourt
options.explanation: Incorrect — Under Art. 30 & Art. 28, backcourt status requires frontcourt team control followed by offensive first touch in backcourt. Official Ruling: Official Case B460 (Backcourt · Art. 30 (Ball Returned to Backcourt)): Backcourt violation? Player 4 has not yet gone into the frontcourt, as he have not yet touched the frontcourt with both feet; therefore, a backcourt violation could not have occurred.

options.optionLabel: C. Double dribble violation — opponents’ throw-in at centre line
options.explanation: Incorrect — No double dribble occurred. Official Ruling: Official Case B460 (Backcourt · Art. 30 (Ball Returned to Backcourt)): Backcourt violation? Player 4 has not yet gone into the frontcourt, as he have not yet touched the frontcourt with both feet; therefore, a backcourt violation could not have occurred.

options.optionLabel: D. 8-second backcourt violation resetting possession
options.explanation: Incorrect — Play stays live — neither 8-second nor backcourt infraction took place. Official Ruling: Official Case B460 (Backcourt · Art. 30 (Ball Returned to Backcourt)): Backcourt violation? Player 4 has not yet gone into the frontcourt, as he have not yet touched the frontcourt with both feet; therefore, a backcourt violation could not have occurred.

title: Case A1176 · Flagrant foul
prompt: Watch video case A1176 (Flagrant foul). Analyze the player positions, timing, and contact/footwork shown in the clip, then select the correct Official FIBA 2026 call.

options.optionLabel: A. Offensive foul on the ball handler — goal cancelled
options.explanation: Incorrect — Excessive/unnecessary contact cannot be left as a normal foul. Official Ruling: Official Case A1176 (Flagrant foul · Art. 37 / Art. 38 (Flagrant & Unsportsmanlike Foul)): Pink 8 causes hard contact. Flagrant foul.

options.optionLabel: B. No-call — clean defensive contest on the ball
options.explanation: Incorrect — Contact clearly passes the threshold for a flagrant/unsportsmanlike upgrade. Official Ruling: Official Case A1176 (Flagrant foul · Art. 37 / Art. 38 (Flagrant & Unsportsmanlike Foul)): Pink 8 causes hard contact. Flagrant foul.

options.optionLabel: C. Flagrant / Unsportsmanlike foul (Art. 38) — 2 free throws + throw-in at frontcourt throw-in line; counts toward GD
options.explanation: Correct — Official Case A1176 (Flagrant foul · Art. 37 / Art. 38 (Flagrant & Unsportsmanlike Foul)): Pink 8 causes hard contact. Flagrant foul.

options.optionLabel: D. Normal personal foul — non-shooting throw-in or standard shooting FTs only
options.explanation: Incorrect — Excessive, hard, dangerous, or non-basketball contact meets Art. 38 Flagrant/Unsportsmanlike criteria. Official Ruling: Official Case A1176 (Flagrant foul · Art. 37 / Art. 38 (Flagrant & Unsportsmanlike Foul)): Pink 8 causes hard contact. Flagrant foul.

title: Case A1177 · Act of shooting
ruleReference: Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)
prompt: Video Case A1177 (Act of shooting): Foul during the act of shooting. Due to the foul the shooter momentarily loses control of the ball, regains control and scores. Would you count the basket? Watch the clip and choose the correct ruling.

options.optionLabel: A. Offensive foul — basket cancelled and turnover
options.explanation: Incorrect — The defender, not the shooter, committed the illegal contact. Official Ruling: Official Case A1177 (Act of shooting · Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)): Foul during the act of shooting. Due to the foul the shooter momentarily loses control of the ball, regains control and scores. Would you count the basket? OBRI 15-10 Example: B1 fouls A1 on a drive to the basket, with A1’s front foot still on the court. A1 continues the act of shooting and because of B1’s foul, the ball momentarily leaves A1’s hands. A1 catches the ball with both hands and scores a goal. Interpretation: B1’s foul against A1 occurred in the act of shooting. When the ball momentarily leaves A1’s hands, A1 still remains in control of the ball and therefore the act of shooting continues. The goal shall count. A1 shall attempt 1 free throw. The game shall continue as after any last free throw.

options.optionLabel: B. Foul in the act of shooting — goal COUNTS + 1 bonus free throw (Art. 15)
options.explanation: Correct — Official Case A1177 (Act of shooting · Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)): Foul during the act of shooting. Due to the foul the shooter momentarily loses control of the ball, regains control and scores. Would you count the basket? OBRI 15-10 Example: B1 fouls A1 on a drive to the basket, with A1’s front foot still on the court. A1 continues the act of shooting and because of B1’s foul, the ball momentarily leaves A1’s hands. A1 catches the ball with both hands and scores a goal. Interpretation: B1’s foul against A1 occurred in the act of shooting. When the ball momentarily leaves A1’s hands, A1 still remains in control of the ball and therefore the act of shooting continues. The goal shall count. A1 shall attempt 1 free throw. The game shall continue as after any last free throw.

options.optionLabel: C. Non-shooting foul — goal cancelled, sideline throw-in only
options.explanation: Incorrect — Under Art. 15, once the upward shooting motion begins and continues cleanly through release, the goal counts plus 1 FT. Official Ruling: Official Case A1177 (Act of shooting · Art. 15 (Player in the Act of Shooting)): Foul during the act of shooting. Due to the foul the shooter momentarily loses control of the ball, regains control and scores. Would you count the basket? OBRI 15-10 Example: B1 fouls A1 on a drive to the basket, with A1’s front foot still on the court. A1 continues the act of shooting and because of B1’s foul, the ball momentarily leaves A1’s hands. A1 catches the ball with both hands and scores a goal. Interpretation: B1’s foul against A1 occurred in the act of shooting. When the ball momentarily leaves A1’s hands, A1 still remains in control of the ball and therefore the act of shooting continues. The goal shall count. A1 shall attempt 1 free throw. The game shall continue as after any last free throw.

options.optionLabel: D. Foul before the shot — 2 free throws, basket cancelled
options.explanation: Incorrect — The foul occurred after the act of shooting had already started.
